title: NFL reportedly wants Paramount to increase rights fee north of 50-60 percent
article_text:
The incumbent NFL broadcasters may end up paying at least 50 percent more — amounting to in excess of $3.0 billion a year each — simply to keep their rights through the end of the originally negotiated terms.

The NFL is seeking a rights fee increase north of 50-60 percent as part of its media rights negotiations with CBS parent company Paramount Skydance, with that range representing the “midpoint” between what the league is seeking and what it is currently being offered, according to Alex Sherman of CNBC. A 50 percent increase would raise the current CBS rights fee of $2.1 billion/year past the $3 billion mark.

As John Ourand of Puck reported last week, the new rights fees will kick in immediately upon the completion of any deal. The league is expected to negotiate its renewals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, per Ourand.

The new report Friday was the first concrete indication of where the NFL might set the market for its expedited media rights negotiations. A 50 percent increase across the board would take each of the league’s broadcast network rights deals past the $3 billion mark, with Disney paying more than $4 billion. But Amazon, which is paying just $1.0 billion/year for its main “Thursday Night Football” package, would still be paying less than $2 billion.

There is no reason to believe the NFL would seek consistent increases across the board, as it has not done so in past negotiations. In the 2011 media rights talks, Disney agreed to pay nearly twice as much for NFL rights ($1.9B/year) as any of the other networks (FOX was second-highest a $1.1B/year). When those rights were renewed in 2021, CBS, NBC and FOX saw their rights fees double, while Disney — which remained the highest-paying rightsholder — came away with a comparably modest 40 percent increase. One can envision a repeat in the upcoming negotiations, as it is hard to imagine that Prime Video will continue paying half as much as the other networks.

Notably, any eventual deal cannot be accurately described as a media rights ‘extension.’ Per Sherman, the NFL is agreeing only to waive the opt-out provision it could otherwise exercise in 2029. And while it has long been assumed that the NFL would exercise that opt-out, the fact is that those 2021 media rights deals were always set to run through the 2033-34 season. In agreeing to negotiate early, the networks are merely guaranteeing that they will have rights for as long as was originally negotiated.

title: Lakers ink sponsorship deal with Kalshi
article_text: The Lakers have named Kalshi the team’s official prediction market sponsor. Kalshi is an NBA preferred prediction market exchange (Lakers). The Lakers become the second NBA team to have signed a deal in that category after the 76ers signed Kalshi as their official prediction market sponsor. The Hawks had signed PrizePicks as a sponsor, making it the first pick ‘em and prediction market operator to sponsor an NBA team, but its deal precluded it from promoting its prediction market offerings through the Hawks (SBJ).

title: Rights to next WBC will be negotiated alongside broader MLB package
article_text:
Coming off of a record-setting performance in the United States, negotiations for rights to the next World Baseball Classic will coincide with Major League Baseball’s broader media rights talks.

Rights to broadcast the next World Baseball Classic will be negotiated alongside the broader Major League Baseball rights packages in 2028, Sports Media Watch has learned. WBC rights have historically been sold separately, but MLB will have the opportunity to add the WBC to conversations that are already expected to include its full suite of local, national and global rights.

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred signaled as much on “The Dan Patrick Show” earlier this month: “Our broadcast partners were out in force at the WBC finals and I think this is going to be a piece of our national broadcasting agreements.”

Manfred conditioned that statement on the event shifting to a regular rotation: “Obviously to do that it has to be on a regular schedule.” The WBC has taken place every three or four years since its inception in 2006, and it is not immediately clear whether the next edition will be in 2029 or 2030.

Rights to this past year’s WBC were officially set mere months in advance, with Fox Sports’ deal to acquire U.S. rights announced last October. It is unclear whether the company had any competition for the event, which ended up delivering audiences in the neighborhood of World Series games.

Netflix had previously secured Japanese rights to the event in a deal announced last August.

Both Fox and Netflix are incumbent MLB rights partners and will presumably be at the negotiating table in 2028. There are six total incumbents heading into 2028, with Fox and Netflix joined by NBCUniversal, TNT Sports, Apple and ESPN — the latter of which was the initial English-language broadcast partner for the WBC in 2006 and 2009.

MLB also has a partnership with TelevisaUnivision, which has carried Game 1 of the World Series in each of the past two seasons and this past year shared WBC rights in Mexico with Disney.

The league is also widely expected to at least attempt to bundle its full suite of local rights into a centralized package, presumably drawing streamers to the table who do not currently own rights.

title: Major League Fishing Announces Multi-Year Sponsorship Renewal with Tackle Warehouse
article_text:
BENTON, Ky. (Nov. 24, 2026) – Major League Fishing (MLF) announced today a multiyear sponsorship renewal with Tackle Warehouse, a leading online retailer of fishing tackle and equipment. The three-year agreement extends the companies’ longstanding partnership, with Tackle Warehouse continuing as the title sponsor of the Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit and an Official Tackle Retailer of MLF5.

A valued MLF partner since 2020, Tackle Warehouse has played an integral role in supporting competitive bass fishing across multiple levels of the sport. The renewed agreement reinforces the retailer’s commitment to tournament anglers while maintaining its prominent presence throughout MLF’s professional and grassroots tournament platforms.

The 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit will showcase top professional anglers competing across six premier fisheries for the sport’s biggest payouts outside of the Bass Pro Tour, valuable points toward Pro Circuit Championship qualification and opportunities to advance to REDCREST and the Bass Pro Tour.

“Tournament fishing has always been an important part of who we are at Tackle Warehouse, and our partnership with Major League Fishing allows us to stay closely connected to the action and help drive this sport forward,” said Joey Reggio, General Manager at Tackle Warehouse. “We’re proud to back a circuit that gives anglers a real shot at their dreams and gives fans a front-row seat to some of the best tournament bass fishing anywhere.  We’re anglers ourselves, and we’re excited to keep supporting the sport we love.”

Tackle Warehouse will maintain brand visibility across all MLF5 media platforms, including television airings on VICE TV and MLFNOW! livestream coverage on MajorLeagueFishing.com, the MyOutdoorTV (MOTV) app and Rumble, providing opportunities to showcase Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories to the tournament fishing community.

“Tackle Warehouse has been a tremendous partner to Major League Fishing and a trusted resource for our anglers, whether they’re gearing up for their first BFL or preparing for a Pro Circuit event,” said Jake Wittkop, MLF Vice President and Managing Director of Sponsorship and Business Development. “Their continued investment in the Pro Circuit and MLF5 helps give anglers the opportunity to compete close to home and work their way up to the national stage. We’re proud to build on this partnership over the next three years.”

The Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit kicks off Feb. 18-20 at Lake Murray in Columbia, South Carolina, before traveling to Chickamauga Lake in Tennessee, Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Texas, Clarks Hill Lake in Georgia, the Arkansas River in Oklahoma and the St. Lawrence River in New York. The season will culminate Sept. 10-12 at the Pro Circuit Championship on the James River in Richmond, Virginia.

Anglers who aspire to fish the 2027 Tackle Warehouse Pro Circuit may enter by calling Major League Fishing at 270.252.1000.

For more information about MLF, its tournaments and sponsors, visit MajorLeagueFishing.com. To explore Tackle Warehouse’s extensive selection of fishing tackle, equipment and accessories, visit TackleWarehouse.com .

Tackle Warehouse is the premier online shop for all of your bass angling needs. They provide the industry’s best gear, customer service, in-depth knowledge of products, tips and techniques from pros, as well as fast, efficient shipping. For more information visit TackleWarehouse.com   and follow them on social media at Facebook, X,  YouTube  and Instagram.

title: When Everton fans will get first glimpse of new multi-year sponsorship agreement
article_text:
Everton have made an out-of-window signing that is hoped will be a long-term success.

The Toffees have made a number of branding changes in the 2026-27 season already.

CMC Markets took centre stage as the team's new front-of-shirt sponsor, replacing the previous occupier of that position, Stake.

In a resulting move, Stake switched to find their sponsorship place on the sleeves of Everton shirts.

This was done as part of Everton's compliance with the Premier League's new front-of-shirt gambling ban.

Hill Dickinson Stadium chiefs have evidently been continuing to search for fresh commercial agreements, and they've now struck another one.

What benefits will Everton's new sponsor get from partnership deal?

Announced via Everton's club website on Tuesday afternoon, the club have signed a 'multi-year' partnership deal with global technology brand, NOCO.

No concrete details have yet emerged on the figures and fees involved in the agreement.

However, with the company signing on to join Everton for a number of years, it's clearly an important business deal for the club.

Confirming via their website, Everton have revealed that NOCO will receive "prominent brand visibility" around Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Their presence will be seen on advertising boards surrounding the pitch, as well as promotion through Everton's various media channels.

NOCO branding will first appear at an Everton matchday on Sunday, when the latest renewal of the Merseyside derby takes place against Liverpool.

So, who exactly are NOCO, and what official partner are they becoming for Everton?

Why TFG have takeover incentives to cash in on multiple Everton players in January Where are Everton's new sponsors NOCO based?

Founded in Cleveland, Ohio in 1914, NOCO are now headquartered in Glenwillow, Ohio.

They are a privately held American multinational corporation, who largely specialise in the designing, manufacturing and marketing of electronic products.

NOCO are predominantly known for their production of battery chargers and lithium batteries, but produce many other related products.

It's probably no surprise then that they've become Everton's new official battery charging partner.

Of course, this deal represents a fresh wave of American financial investment into Everton alongside The Friedkin Group.

Whether or not this is a targeted and deliberate move by Everton in a wider attempt to increase their standing across the pond, or a coincidence, remains to be seen.

What it should do at a base level is increase the selling value of the football club, as TFG continue to explore a sale.

However, with this deal being announced off the back of Everton's 4-0 thrashing to Brentford, fans may not be overly thrilled by the timing.

title: Perfect Game expands youth baseball platform into GCC
article_text:
Perfect Game, the world’s largest youth baseball and softball platform and scouting service, has announced its expansion into the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region, naming VICE Baseball as its Country Partner for the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait.

The announcement comes one week after Perfect Game revealed its new partnership in China, continuing the organisation’s international growth.

Beginning in December 2026, VICE will roll out Perfect Game tournaments, clinics and showcases across all four countries.

Dubai will host the first event, followed by a major international tournament in March 2027 that will bring together teams from around the world.

The goal is to strengthen the region’s baseball community and give young athletes more opportunities to compete and showcase their skills in front of scouts.

VICE Baseball, a subsidiary of VICE Sports Group led by Tony Khoury, is a US-based youth baseball development organisation with roots in Katy, Texas.

As Perfect Game’s partner across the GCC, VICE will pair its player development experience with Perfect Game’s established tournament and scouting platform.

VICE’s baseball operations are led by David McDaniel, who brings more than 20 years of coaching experience.

McDaniel played professionally as a catcher in the Cleveland Indians, Detroit Tigers and Texas Rangers organisations.

He later coached with the Sugar Land Skeeters (now the Sugar Land Space Cowboys) and helped guide Texas high school teams to state championships.

His approach emphasises sound fundamentals, game awareness and leadership to prepare players for higher levels of competition.

Kash Shaikh, Perfect Game’s Chief Marketing Officer and Head of International, is the former chairman, CEO and co-founder of Dubai-based Baseball United.

"It’s very special to be able to bring more baseball back to Dubai, Saudi, and the surrounding GCC region. After spending the last four years in Dubai working to build the baseball ecosystem with my previous league, I realised that we needed to do more to help a greater number of young athletes fall in love with the game," said Shaikh.

"With PG and our partnership with VICE, we will now offer families across the region access to top tournaments, international events and the best baseball scouting platform in the world. There are a lot of people already doing great work in the baseball community, and we are looking forward to partnering with them to make it all happen," he added.

VICE will work with local baseball organisations, academies and teams to build a regular event calendar and encourage participation across age groups.

Showcases will give players a chance to demonstrate their skills and gain visibility through Perfect Game’s international platform.

The long-term goal is a sustainable regional circuit that brings baseball communities together, raises the level of competition and gives young athletes a clearer path to advance in the sport.

"Our partnership with Perfect Game marks a milestone for youth baseball in the GCC. It puts a spotlight on the talent here and gives young players a new platform to compete at a higher level and showcase their skills," said Khoury.

"College coaches and professional scouts will have direct access to player profiles and stats through Perfect Game, and we expect some to attend future events in the region. That gives our players the same kind of scouting exposure as players in the US. We’re grateful for Perfect Game’s trust in VICE and the chance to build something lasting for players and families across the region."

Event dates, locations and registration details will be announced at PerfectGame.org.

title: Maincast Sport secures WTA broadcast rights in Ukraine
article_text:
Maincast Sport has acquired the rights to broadcast the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in Ukraine under a long-term agreement, bringing the world's leading women's professional tennis tour to Ukrainian audiences with dedicated Ukrainian-language coverage.

The agreement will give fans access to Ukrainian-language coverage of WTA tournaments throughout the 2027 season, as the Tour visits 26 countries and territories. From Brisbane and Auckland in January, the season will take in iconic destinations including Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Rome and Beijing, culminating in the season-ending FAGE WTA Finals in Charlotte, USA, in November.

The WTA Tour joins Maincast Sport’s portfolio of international sports properties including the NBA, Copa del Rey, MotoGP and NASCAR. Now with the WTA, the addition further strengthens Maincast Sport’s offering, bringing fans world-class women’s tennis and the opportunity to follow the Ukrainian players who consistently compete at the highest level.

The partnership includes: International WTA 1000 events, WTA 500 Events, WTA 250 Events, and the FAGE WTA Finals taking place in Charlotte (USA), where the season’s top eight singles players and doubles teams will compete.

“Tennis is one of the sports where Ukraine has genuine stars, and fans have followed every match our players have played for years. From 2027, matches featuring Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk, Dayana Yastremska and other Ukrainian players will be available exclusively on Maincast Sport, alongside hundreds of matches from the world’s best players. We’re creating our own tennis shows, analysis and broadcasts with star guests. The WTA calendar runs almost all year round, so Maincast Sport viewers will get top-level tennis every week,,” said Vitalii Volochai, co-founder of Maincast.

“We’re delighted to partner with Maincast Sport to bring more women’s tennis to fans in Ukraine, where the sport already means so much. Ukrainian players continue to make an important impact on the global stage, and this agreement will give fans more opportunities to follow their favourite athletes and experience the excitement of the WTA Tour throughout the season,” said Marina Storti, CEO of WTA Ventures.

WTA Tour matches will be available to fans on the Maincast Sport TV channel and Maincast.tv platform.

title: NASCAR Sponsorship Fallout Grows as Federal Investigation Uncovers Shocking Allegations
article_text:
New details in federal court filings have raised fresh questions about the alleged misuse of investor money connected to Droplight and motorsports sponsorships. A Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) complaint alleges that Phillip Williams, co-founder of Droplight, used more than $11 million in investor funds for an “apparent auto racing team.”

The filing does not identify the team. Motorsports reporter Bob Pockrass of FOX Sports also highlighted an alleged $500,000 payment for an “apparent auto racing sponsorship” linked to Williams’ associate Devin Johnson. The allegations form part of a wider investigation into Backward Hat Capital, which authorities claim raised more than $550 million from investors through a Ponzi-style scheme. Williams and Johnson were arrested on November 18.

The CFTC complaint alleges that more than $11 million in investor funds went toward an apparent auto racing team. It also claims Devin Johnson spent $500,000 from the same pool of money on an apparent racing sponsorship. However, investigators have not named the teams involved in either transaction.

The alleged motorsports spending forms part of a wider list of transfers that authorities say involved investor money. The complaint also lists more than $3.2 million in apparent real estate purchases, $3 million paid to an apparent bare-knuckle fighting promoter, and more than $1.8 million for luxury car garage space.

The CFTC alleges that these payments involved money belonging to participants in the Backward Hat Capital enterprise. The allegations remain unproven and have not been tested at trial.

Federal authorities allege that Backward Hat Capital raised more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants beginning around July 2022. The enterprise allegedly promised monthly returns exceeding 6% with no losing months through leveraged foreign-exchange trading.

However, prosecutors claim little to no actual forex trading took place. Instead, the alleged scheme used money from new investors to pay earlier participants, while large sums went to the people behind the operation.

The criminal complaint alleges that more than $200 million went toward investor redemptions. Authorities also claim accounts controlled by Williams received more than $130 million, while accounts connected to Johnson received over $40 million.

Williams and Johnson were arrested on November 18. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York charged them with securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and conspiracy to commit securities fraud.

Droplight built a presence in motorsports during 2025, sponsoring Louis Foster’s No. 45 Honda at Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing, including the Indianapolis 500. RLL later announced a long-term extension with the company.

The brand also appeared in the NASCAR Truck Series and other racing categories through related sponsorships. Johnson’s company SalesAi separately sponsored Dreyer & Reinbold Racing’s No. 24 entry in recent Indianapolis 500 events, although that connection does not appear in the regulatory allegations.

The SEC has filed a separate civil lawsuit and secured a court-ordered freeze on assets. Its complaint identifies Droplight LLC as a relief defendant and alleges the company received $31 million originating from Backward Hat investors through KMAP Inc.

Following the arrests, Droplight disappeared from RLL’s listed partners, and its websites went offline. Racing teams are reviewing their agreements as the cases move forward. The court filings have not identified the teams connected to the alleged $11 million and $500,000 racing expenditures, leaving those sponsorship details unresolved.

title: Baller League launches international women’s competition
article_text:
Baller League has introduced a women’s competition as part of its new Nations Cup, creating an international six-a-side tournament for amateur female players across 16 countries and 64 cities.

The women’s tournament will run alongside a men’s competition, with both winning teams receiving equal $1m prizes. Teams will progress from city-level tournaments to national qualifiers before the 16 national champions compete at the international finals.

The format will allow amateur teams to enter without affiliation to a professional club, academy or agent. Registration is scheduled to open in March 2027, with the competition running from 26th June until the final weekend from 5th-7th November.

The introduction of the women’s tournament represents an expansion of Baller League’s existing six-a-side format. Founded in Germany in 2024, the competition has since established leagues in the UK and United States.

The equal prize allocation means a combined $2m will be awarded to the men’s and women’s champions. Baller League founder and CEO Felix Starck has described each $1m award as what the organisation believes to be the largest prize offered to amateur footballers, although that claim has not been independently verified.

For the UK, the Nations Cup will build on Baller League’s existing domestic presence and provide amateur women’s teams with a route from local competition to representing their country in an international tournament.

title: Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images Launch Inclusive Community Sport Visual Library
article_text:
The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) has partnered with global visual content creator Getty Images to launch a dedicated visual library designed to modernise how grassroots sport is represented across Australia.

The collection is delivered under Play Well, Australia’s first national sport participation strategy, co-designed with the sector in 2023, and debuts with 250 authentic still images and videos spanning athletics, equestrian, netball, badminton, and football. By resolving a long-standing marketing bottleneck for national sporting organisations (NSOs) and local clubs, the initiative supplies sector-wide communications teams with representative promotional assets ahead of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

ASC executive general manager of sport system impact and chair of the Play Well Leadership Group, Richard McInnes, highlighted the commercial and participation impact of equipping sports with authentic visual storytelling tools.

“Play Well is built on the belief that everyone has a place in sport.”

“We know the way sport is represented can influence whether people feel welcome and believe there is a place for them.

“This partnership will give sporting organisations access to authentic images, to use in promotional material and communication, that actually reflects the diversity of the people, communities and experiences that make Australian sport so special.

“It is another practical step towards breaking down barriers to participation and ensuring more people can see themselves being involved in sport,” McInnes said.

Getty Images senior director of custom and creative partnerships, Svetlana Zhukova, emphasised the role of representative media in reshaping community perceptions ahead of Brisbane 2032.

“Sport has an extraordinary ability to connect people, but the images used to represent it don’t always reflect who is actually taking part.”

“Through the partnership, we’re giving sports organisations, media and communities access to imagery that better reflects the diversity of Australian sport as the country looks towards Brisbane 2032,” Zhukova said.

Produced in collaboration with community clubs and inclusion bodies—including Sport Inclusion Australia, Metropolitan Districts Netball Association, Footscray Rangers Football Club, and Melbourne Smashers Badminton, the library reflects diverse ages, cultural backgrounds, genders, and physical abilities. Sporting bodies and sector partners can request direct access to the asset bank via the ASC marketing team, with additional sports scheduled for production and integration throughout 2027.

title: Arab Cup Qatar 2025 wins Premier Sports Event of the Year Award
article_text:
The FIFA Arab Cup Qatar 2025 won the Qatar Tourism Award for Premier Sports Event of the Year, in recognition of the tournament's outstanding success, strong fan turnout, and contributions to Qatar's economy and tourism sector.

The Local Organizing Committee for Football Events received the award at a ceremony held in Doha, which recognized leading events that have helped strengthen Qatar's position as a premier destination for hosting major sporting events.

The tournament was held from Dec 1 to 18, 2025, with 16 Arab national teams competing across six stadiums that had previously hosted matches during the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022. A total of 1,220,063 fans attended the 32 matches. The final, held at Lusail Stadium, drew 84,517 spectators, setting a record for the highest attendance in the tournament's history.

The tournament's success extended beyond the sporting arena and fan engagement to include a boost to tourism and economic activity. An economic impact assessment conducted in collaboration with Nielsen Sports, a company specializing in sports analytics, found that the tournament generated a total economic impact of QR2.89 billion for the local economy.

The tournament formed part of an exceptional football season in Qatar in 2025, during which the country hosted the finals of three FIFA competitions within three weeks. These included the inaugural 48-team edition of the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup.

Qatar is currently hosting the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 and is preparing to host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, scheduled for Dec 9, 12 and 16.

Qatar continues to strengthen its presence on the global sporting stage by hosting a series of major international competitions, including the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027, the FIFA Arab Cup 2029, the FIVB Volleyball World Championship 2029 and the Asian Games 2030.
